theme.title: Hakeem's Rockets
theme.subtitle: Houston, 1993–95
theme.recap: Houston started 15–0, won a seven-game Finals against New York and then won another title as a sixth seed.

questions.prompt: The 1993–94 Rockets opened the season with how many straight wins?
questions.note: 15, tying the record at the time.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: winning their first fifteen games of the regular season to tie the

funFacts.text: Houston used its 1993 first-round draft pick on point guard Sam Cassell, who had played at Florida State.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Rockets had the 24th overall pick in the 1993 NBA draft, and selected point guard Sam Cassell out of Florida State University.

funFacts.text: The Rockets also added Mario Elie from Portland in the offseason before their first championship.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: During the off-season, the team acquired Mario Elie from the Portland Trail Blazers.

funFacts.text: The 1994 Finals victory was the first major championship for a Houston team in a professional league that still existed.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: This was the first major professional sports championship ever won by a Houston-based team.

questions.prompt: Patrick Ewing set a Finals record for blocks in a series in 1994. How many?
questions.context: 1994 NBA Finals · seven games vs Houston

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Ewing set an NBA finals record in the series with a total of 30 blocks

funFacts.text: The 1994 series was Patrick Ewing's first appearance in the NBA Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The series was Patrick Ewing's first NBA Finals appearance.

funFacts.text: Ewing and Olajuwon had already met for a title in college: Georgetown beat the University of Houston in the 1984 NCAA championship.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In 1984, while Olajuwon was with the University of Houston and Ewing was with Georgetown University, Georgetown beat Houston 84–75

funFacts.text: Hakeem Olajuwon earned both league MVP and Defensive Player of the Year honors during the Rockets' title season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Olajuwon won the MVP and Defensive Player of the Year awards at season's end.

questions.prompt: John Starks went 0-for-what from three-point range in Game 7 of the 1994 Finals?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Starks struggled severely, shooting 2-of-18 from the field (0-for-11 from three-point range)

funFacts.text: In the previous game, Olajuwon blocked a last-second Starks three-point attempt that could have clinched New York's first title in decades.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In Game 6, Olajuwon blocked a last-second three-point shot attempt by John Starks

funFacts.text: Starks shot just 2-for-18 from the field in Game 7 overall, not merely missing from beyond the arc.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Starks struggled severely, shooting 2-of-18 from the field

funFacts.text: After the series, Pat Riley said not benching Starks during the decisive game was his biggest coaching mistake of that Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Pat Riley admitted that his biggest mistake of the series was not benching John Starks during Game 7 of the Finals.

questions.prompt: Late in Game 1 of the 1995 Finals, Nick Anderson missed how many free throws in a row?
questions.note: Four, and Houston won in overtime.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Nick Anderson missed four consecutive free throws in the closing seconds of the game

funFacts.text: The Orlando Magic were only in their sixth season as an NBA franchise when they reached that Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Magic were only in their sixth season of existence, but they were a team on the rise.

funFacts.text: After Anderson's misses, Houston's Kenny Smith tied the opener with a three-pointer to force overtime.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kenny Smith hit a three-pointer, tying the game and sending it to overtime

funFacts.text: Houston had brought Clyde Drexler home from Portland in a midseason trade, reuniting him with his college teammate Olajuwon.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Rockets acquired Clyde Drexler from the Portland Trail Blazers, but the trade of a hometown hero

questions.prompt: The 1995 Rockets were the first team to win how many road playoff games in one postseason?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Rockets became the first NBA team to win nine road playoff games

funFacts.text: Houston's path to a repeat championship went through four opponents that had each won at least 50 regular-season games.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Rockets became the first NBA team to win nine road playoff games and to beat four 50-win teams

funFacts.text: The Rockets never had home-court advantage in any of their four playoff rounds that spring.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: to win the title without having home-court advantage in any of the four playoff rounds

funFacts.text: Houston became the first repeat champion to defend its NBA title with a Finals sweep.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Rockets also became the first repeat NBA Champion in history to keep the title with a sweep.
